description: Figure 2 illustrates a set of layer grouping patterns across four groups, showing how the number of layers is allocated to each group under different patterns. The chart uses a horizontal category axis representing the groups \(G_1, G_2, G_3, G_4\) in left-to-right order, and a vertical value axis representing the number of layers in each group (a linear scale is implied, but no numeric tick labels are visible). Within a single light-gray rectangular plotting area, five separate line-and-marker profiles are drawn across the four group positions: each profile consists of black circular markers at each group connected by black line segments, indicating the relative layer counts per group for that pattern. The five profiles include a monotonically increasing profile from \(G_1\) to \(G_4\), a flat (uniform) profile with equal marker heights across all four groups, a monotonically decreasing profile from \(G_1\) to \(G_4\), a “spindle” profile with lower endpoints at \(G_1\) and \(G_4\) and higher middle points at \(G_2\) and \(G_3\), and a “bottleneck” profile with higher endpoints at \(G_1\) and \(G_4\) and lower middle points at \(G_2\) and \(G_3\). No legend, numeric values, bar elements, or explicit sorting cues are shown, and no individual profile is visually emphasized beyond being drawn in the same black style on the gray background.
